title: The other spoon

item.name: Lot 20
item.line: An oak spoon as long as an arm, with 20 names burned into the handle, up for sale on Saturday. The Long Spoon is on its hooks in the hall.

brief: Both signs on the row were painted by 1 practised hand, and nobody will say whose. Then the sale room puts up its list for Saturday.
Lot 20: the Long Spoon, with all 20 names burned into the handle. The Long Spoon is on its hooks in the hall, where it has been since the final.
The art class has been burning letters into oak all term. Bea, who teaches it, says that proves nothing.
1 spoon too many. Prove where it came from.

pins.label: The real one, on its hooks

suspects.name: Bea
suspects.line: Teaches the art class in the room over the bakery. Her pupils have been burning oak all term.
suspects.says: Half the street can burn a letter into wood. That proves nothing.

steps.thing: The sale room the day before the sale. Most of it is lots nobody is asking about.

things.name: The torn page in the bin

steps.fact: Lot 20 is a long oak spoon with 20 names burned on, and its ticket says only Lot 20. The sale book has a page torn out by the spine, and half of a torn page is in the bin.
steps.pin: A page torn from the book
steps.lead: The half in the bin is not enough to read. The other half is still caught in the sale book, by the spine.

steps.thing: The 2 halves of the page, one from the bin and one from the spine of the book. Each line tore in a different place.
page: A copy of the Long Spoon
Made by the art class, 14 pupils
Sold for the art room kiln fund
steps.fact: It is the first entry for lot 20: a copy of the Long Spoon, made by the art class, for the kiln fund. Somebody tore it out. The book took a second entry for lot 20 the same morning, with no word of a copy.
steps.lead: Somebody made a copy, and somebody tore out the word. The art room keeps receipts for everything it buys.

steps.thing: The art room's receipt book. Bea writes in every penny, because the school checks it each term.
steps.fact: On 2 October the art room bought an oak blank 1 metre long and a second burning pen. The kiln fund is 140 short of a new kiln.
steps.lead: The class made it. That is not a crime. The sale room's own log says what happened on Tuesday morning, and 20 minutes of it are missing.

steps.thing: The clerk's log for Tuesday morning, with a gap in it.

events: 10 am. Lot 20 is entered: a copy of the Long Spoon, by the art class.
10.20 am. Lot 20 is entered again: the Long Spoon, 20 names.
Wednesday. The street queues to see the second spoon.

options.text: The real spoon is taken from its hooks and brought in.
The clerk turns the entry down, because the sale room takes no copies, and the page is torn out.
The art class sells the copy to a stranger in the street.

steps.fact: The sale room takes no copies. The first entry was turned down and torn out at 10.05, and at 10.20 the same spoon came back in as itself, entered by the same hand.
steps.lead: Why bring it back as the real thing? Across the art room wall the class has strung its project title in cut out letters.

steps.thing: The class project title, strung across the wall in cut out letters, 1 row with no spaces.
steps.fact: Can the street tell our burns from 20 years of finals? It was a test of the class's hands, and the sale was going to be the exam.
steps.lead: A copy, a word torn out, and a test nobody was told about. 3 accounts are going round the sale room.

steps.thing: 3 accounts of lot 20. Each piece of evidence already on the board strikes 1 of them out.

accounts.text: The Long Spoon was stolen again and put up for sale.
Bea entered her class's copy honestly, and the sale room got the label wrong.
When the sale room would not take a copy, Bea entered it as the real thing, to see if anyone could tell.

steps.fact: Chance: turned down at 10.05, back at 10.20. Means: an oak blank and a second burning pen. Motive: a test of the class's hands.

ending.found: Lot 20 is oak from the art room, burned by 14 pupils with 2 pens. The names are right, every one, down to R. MARLOW 2011, burned back only weeks ago.
ending.confession: Nobody could tell. That was the point. My pupils did in a fortnight what took the street 20 finals, and the sale room would not even let them call it theirs.
ending.after: The lot is withdrawn. The committee wants the copy for a case beside the real one. Asked how the class had all 20 names so soon, Bea shows a letter that came by post: the list, no name, and the lantern card.
